description.value: The study investigated how fluid reasoning complexity modulates cortical activity differently in participants with high versus low fluid intelligence.

spans.text: Our first goal was verifying the probable presence of differential patterns of activation in response to increasing fluid difficulty which might depend on gf variability among individuals.

design.value: Two groups with different fluid intelligence levels performed moderate and complex reasoning tasks and a control task during fMRI; activity was analyzed within and between groups.

spans.text: Then, using fMRI we analyzed the signal variation associated with moderate and complex reasoning items between and within the two samples.

we developed a computerized behavioral task composed by a total of 32 fluid reasoning and 32 control problems adapted from both the RSPM and RAPM.

task_description.value: Participants solved figural and analytic Raven-like matrix problems, interleaved with control matrices.

spans.text: A scanning session consisted of two different runs (for a total of 32 trials), each made up of 8 figural, 8 analytic, and 16 control items.

presentation_software.value: E-Prime software, v.1.1, Psychology Software Tools

spans.text: Presentations of the stimuli were controlled by means of the E-Prime software, v.1.1, Psychology Software Tools running on a PC placed in the scanner console room.

stimuli.value: 3 × 3 matrices containing figural elements, with eight alternatives for the missing lower-right entry; control matrices contained elements devoid of logical relations.

spans.text: Each reasoning problem consisted of a 3 × 3 matrix placed on the left visual field of the subject in which the bottom right entry was missing.

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to solve reasoning problems and watch control problems, and not to guess when necessary.

spans.text: The subject was instructed to take all the time necessary for generating the solution
